## Cumulative performance

Compounded return of each ext-set model against the historical-mean strategy. The dotted line is always T-bills.


## Theoretical best

The strategy that knows the sign of the realised log equity premium, against the historical mean.

```{r performance-best, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
g_perf_best
```

## Final performance

Test-set results for the ext-set models, the historical mean, and the theoretical best. Wealth starts at $1 million. `final_wealth_m` is terminal wealth in millions, and `max_drawdown` is the largest peak-to-trough loss of that wealth, in percent. `pct_in_mkt` is the share of test months the strategy holds the S&P 500. The columns from `n` through `pct_yhat_pos` are the forecast evaluation against the historical mean: out-of-sample R², the Diebold-Mariano test, the hit rate and its benchmark, and the Pesaran-Timmermann test. `pct_yhat_pos` is the share of forecast origins with a positive forecast. It matches `pct_in_mkt` at h = 1; at longer horizons the backtest only acts every h months, so the two can differ. The `hit` cell on the historical-mean rows is that benchmark's own hit rate, the same number as `hit_bench`. The other forecast columns stay blank for the historical mean and the theoretical best, because those two rows are trading rules rather than forecasts scored against a benchmark.

```{r perf-table}
knitr::kable(perf_tbl, digits = 3)
```

## Lasso coefficients

BIC lasso coefficient at every test origin, for both predictor sets and all three horizons. `lasso_coef` is that series: a zero means the penalty dropped the predictor in that window. The table is the share of origins, in percent, in which the coefficient is nonzero.

```{r lasso-coef}
lasso_coef <- read.csv(file.path(TAB_DIR, "lasso_bic_coef.csv"))
lasso_selection <- read.csv(file.path(TAB_DIR, "lasso_bic_selection.csv"))
```

```{r lasso-selection}
knitr::kable(lasso_selection, digits = 0)
```

## Ridge coefficients

Ridge coefficient at every test origin. `std_coef` is the coefficient times the predictor's standard deviation in that window: the change in the forecast for a one-standard-deviation move. The table averages `std_coef` over the test origins. A predictor that is not in the `gw` set is blank in the `gw` columns.

```{r ridge-coef}
ridge_coef <- read.csv(file.path(TAB_DIR, "ridge_coef.csv"))
ridge_coef_summary <- read.csv(file.path(TAB_DIR, "ridge_coef_summary.csv"))
```

```{r ridge-summary}
knitr::kable(ridge_coef_summary, digits = 7)
```

## Random forest importance

Percent rise in out-of-bag MSE when the predictor is shuffled, averaged over the 10 annual tuning dates. `rf_importance` is the ranked table behind these figures.

```{r rf-importance-data}
rf_importance <- read.csv(file.path(TAB_DIR, "rf", "rf_importance_summary.csv"))
```

```{r rf-importance, fig.width=10, fig.height=5.5}
lab1 <- function(x) sub("^-0\\.0$", "0.0", sprintf("%.1f", x))

for (s in c("gw", "ext")) {
  ds <- rf_importance |>
    filter(set == s, rank <= 15) |>
    mutate(hl  = factor(sapply(h, h_lab), levels = sapply(HORIZONS, h_lab)),
           key = factor(paste(feature, h, sep = "___")))
  ds$key <- reorder(ds$key, ds$mean_pct)
  n_vars <- n_distinct(rf_importance$feature[rf_importance$set == s])
  g <- ggplot(ds, aes(mean_pct, key)) +
    geom_col(fill = BLUE, width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = lab1(mean_pct),
                  hjust = ifelse(mean_pct < 0, 1.25, -0.25)),
              size = 3, colour = INK2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = INK2, linewidth = 0.3) +
    facet_wrap(~ hl, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) sub("___.*$", "", x)) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 70), breaks = seq(0, 70, 10),
                       expand = c(0, 0), oob = scales::oob_keep) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(1.5, "lines"),
          plot.margin = margin(5.5, 20, 5.5, 5.5)) +
    labs(title = sprintf("Random forest permutation importance (out-of-bag) - %s predictor set", s),
         subtitle = paste0("% rise in out-of-bag MSE when the variable is shuffled, ",
                           "averaged over the 10 annual tuning dates",
                           if (n_vars > 15) sprintf(" | top 15 of %d shown", n_vars) else ""),
         x = "Rise in OOB MSE (%)", y = NULL)
  print(g)
}
```

## XGBoost importance

Gain averaged over the same 10 tuning dates, square-rooted and scaled so the top predictor in each panel is 100. `xgb_importance` is that summary.

```{r xgb-importance-data}
xgb_importance <- read.csv(file.path(TAB_DIR, "xgb_importance_summary.csv"))
```

```{r xgb-importance, fig.width=10, fig.height=5.5}
for (s in c("gw", "ext")) {
  ds <- xgb_importance |>
    filter(set == s, rank <= 15) |>
    mutate(hl  = factor(sapply(h, h_lab), levels = sapply(HORIZONS, h_lab)),
           key = factor(paste(feature, h, sep = "___")))
  ds$key <- reorder(ds$key, ds$rel_importance)
  g <- ggplot(ds, aes(rel_importance, key)) +
    geom_col(fill = BLUE, width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(rel_importance)), hjust = -0.25, size = 3, colour = INK2) +
    facet_wrap(~ hl, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) sub("___.*$", "", x)) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 112), breaks = c(0, 50, 100), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(title = sprintf("XGBoost relative importance - %s predictor set", s),
         subtitle = paste("sqrt(average gain over the 10 annual tuning dates), most",
                          "important variable = 100", if (s == "ext") "| top 15 shown" else ""),
         x = "Relative importance", y = NULL)
  print(g)
}
```
